name: Standard Lithium Ltd. (NYSE American: SLI, TSXV: SLI)
analyst_actions: 2026-09-14 | Roth MKM | Reiterates Buy | Buy->Buy, price target 5.25 USD
2026-09-02 | Jefferies | Initiates Coverage Hold | none->Hold, price target 2.90 USD
consensus_source: https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/sli/forecast/ (S&P Global poll, 6 analysts, mean 4.51 USD); https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSEAMERICAN/SLI/price-target/ (5 analysts, mean 5.16 USD)
upcoming_dates: 2026-09-29 | investor conference | Lytham Partners Fall 2026 Investor Conference, virtual, Sep 29 to Sep 30 2026 | https://www.standardlithium.com/investors/events/ | primary
product: Battery-grade lithium carbonate produced from Smackover Formation brine using direct lithium extraction and purification, at the South West Arkansas Project and the Franklin Project in East Texas, with potential bromine and potash by-products.
demand: Company cites global lithium demand reaching 3.3 million tonnes LCE by 2030, more than double 2025 levels, and has converted demand into binding take-or-pay contracts covering roughly 90 percent of targeted SWA offtake with LG Energy Solution and Trafigura.
pricing_power: Limited: the LG Energy Solution contract prices the product off a monthly average price index with confidentiality on terms, so lithium price risk passes through to the seller rather than being captured as economic rent. Commercial traction with two blue-chip buyers is the positive signal.
competition: Global brine and hard-rock lithium producers, other Smackover Formation DLE developers in Arkansas and Texas, and a Chinese-dominated supply chain. Standard Lithium positions US-produced, non-China supply and DOE backing as the differentiation (Sep 8 2026 PEA).
team: CEO David Park, President and COO Dr. Andy Robinson, CFO Salah Gamoudi, Independent Chairman Bob Cross. Nine directors elected Jul 16 2026 with roughly 99 percent support each; board reduced to eight after Karen Narwold resigned effective Sep 15 2026, with a search for a new independent director underway.
market_strategy: Operate a 55/45 partnership, Smackover Lithium, with Equinor holding 45 percent and Standard Lithium the operator. Pair index-linked take-or-pay offtakes with export-credit-agency project debt and a USD 225M DOE grant, take FID in 2026, then scale East Texas toward well over 100,000 t/yr.
bull: Binding take-or-pay offtakes with LG Energy Solution (Aug 31 2026) and Trafigura cover ~90% of SWA volume; NEPA FONSI, EPCC/EPCM signed, USD 137.3M cash and no debt; Roth MKM reiterated Buy with USD 5.25 target Sep 14 2026.
bear: Pre-revenue, no cash flow before 2029; USD 3.5B Franklin capex against USD 137.3M cash; FID slipped; shares fell ~37% in 63 days to USD 2.06; ATM shares sold at USD 3.59, so dilution at falling prices is the visible failure mode.
falsifier: No Final Investment Decision on the South West Arkansas Project announced by December 31 2026, or an equity raise priced below USD 2.06 before FID.
web_what_changed: Jul 16 2026 AGM elected nine directors and PwC as auditor. Aug 10 2026 Q2: NEPA Finding of No Significant Impact for SWA; EPCC signed with S&B Engineers and Constructors plus Hatch; EPCM with Wood Group USA; cash USD 137.3M, no debt. Aug 31 2026 LG Energy Solution 8,000 t/yr ten-year offtake. Sep 8 2026 Franklin Texas PEA. Sep 15 2026 director Karen Narwold resigned.
web_not_known_yesterday: not found. No new company disclosure since the Sep 21 2026 6-K; the newest investor-relations press release on the company site is dated Sep 11 2026, and no wire story dated Sep 24 or Sep 25 2026 was located.
web_demand_price_volume_mix: Pre-revenue developer, so no current revenue mix. Future growth is volume-led: SWA nameplate 22,500 t/yr initial phase and Franklin up to 70,000 t/yr. Contract price is a monthly average price index, so price is pass-through rather than company pricing uplift (Aug 31 and Sep 10 2026).
web_suppliers: Disclosed: EPCC for the SWA central processing facility by S&B Engineers and Constructors, supported by Hatch; EPCM for the wellfield by Wood Group USA; process and water technology partner Aquatech. Both contracts carry Limited Notice to Proceed (Aug 10 2026). No disclosed supplier constraint found.
web_customers: Highly concentrated: LG Energy Solution, 8,000 t/yr battery-grade lithium carbonate over 10 years, binding take-or-pay, contract effective Aug 27 2026; and Trafigura, 8,000 t/yr over 10 years, announced Mar 9 2026. Together roughly 90 percent of the targeted offtake volume, about 80 percent of the 22,500 t initial nameplate.
web_who_loses: Aggregator context only: Chinese lithium carbonate producers and converters that dominate the global supply chain, plus rival Smackover and US DLE developers competing for the same brine, offtake customers and DOE or export-credit support. No primary source quantified a loss for any named competitor.
web_contradicting_evidence: Shares closed USD 2.06 on Sep 24 2026, down about 37 percent over 63 days, far below targets. Jefferies initiated Hold with a USD 2.90 target on Sep 2 2026, framing value as long-dated optionality. No revenue expected before 2029; Franklin starts in the early 2030s. USD 3.5B Franklin capex versus USD 137.3M cash. FID slipped.
web_if_management_right: Final Investment Decision on the SWA Project by year-end 2026, construction starting promptly, first commercial battery-grade lithium carbonate in 2029, roughly 90 percent offtake committed with over USD 1B of export-credit-agency debt indications and a USD 225M DOE grant, then more than 100,000 t/yr across East Texas projects including Franklin.
web_if_management_wrong: Project financing breaks first: without ECA debt and further equity the SWA Project cannot reach FID, pushing first revenue past 2029 and delaying Franklin. The USD 50M at-the-market facility already sold shares at an average USD 3.59 in Q2 2026 versus USD 2.06 now, so continued dilution at falling prices is the visible failure mode.
web_second_order_beneficiaries: Nano One Materials (LFP cathode validation, Aug 13 2026); Equinor as 45 percent partner; contractors S&B Engineers and Constructors, Hatch and Wood Group; Aquatech; offtakers Trafigura and LG Energy Solution; and Arkansas and East Texas labor and services supply chains.
